title: An unramified morphism is quasi-finite at every point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then $f$ is quasi-finite at every point $x\in X$ in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1): there are an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A=U\subseteq X$ containing $x$ and an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R=V\subseteq S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $f(U)\subseteq V$ such that $R\to A$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ corresponding to $x$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]: with $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the prime below $\mathfrak q$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ its residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ is an isolated point. In other words, $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02V5 (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite), lines 7779-7788; its proof is Algebra, Lemma 02UR (algebra.tex, lemma-unramified-quasi-finite, line 41599), which uses Algebra, Lemma 00PK (lemma-isolated-point-fibre, line 30196) part (2) and Lemma 00UW (lemma-unramified-at-prime, line 41568)

proof.text: Fix x in X. Mathlib exists_isAffineOpen_mem_and_subset first supplies an affine open V containing f(x), then an affine open U containing x and contained in f inverse V. Equip the map on sections with its induced algebra structure. Mathlib Scheme.Hom.finiteType_appLE supplies Algebra.FiniteType. The open-diagonal instance supplies FormallyUnramified f, and Scheme.Hom.formallyUnramified_appLE supplies Algebra.FormallyUnramified on these same section rings.

Mathlib.RingTheory.Unramified.LocalStructure has the instance [EssFiniteType R A] [FormallyUnramified R A] : Algebra.QuasiFinite R A. FiniteType supplies EssFiniteType. Hence each fibre ring over a prime p is module-finite over its residue field, by Algebra.QuasiFinite.finite_fiber. The instance Algebra.QuasiFinite.instIsArtinianRingFiber makes the fibre Artinian, and Mathlib gives its prime spectrum the discrete topology. This uses no finite-product decomposition or deferred project theorem.

At q corresponding to x, unfold Algebra.IsQuasiFiniteAtPrime. Its fibre point is the image of q under PrimeSpectrum.preimageHomeomorphFiber. Since the entire fibre spectrum is discrete, isOpen_discrete proves that its singleton is open. Package the affine opens, containment, and finite-type witness in IsQuasiFiniteAtPoint f x. As x was arbitrary this proves IsLocallyQuasiFinite f.

Source place corrected: 00UW (not 00UV) is lemma-unramified-at-prime, 00PK (not 00PJ) is lemma-isolated-point-fibre. Proof in four steps following Algebra 02UR with the proof of 00UW: (1) affine charts, restriction unramified (lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open (2)) and Spec-to-ring translation (leaf lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine): R->A finite type with Omega=0; (2) fibre ring F=A(x)kappa(p) finitely generated with Omega=0 by the leaf lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change, hence Spec F -> Spec kappa(p) unramified; (3) F is a finite product of finite separable extensions (lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product) so Spec F is discrete (lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields (2)); (4) the prime of F over q (lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection) is isolated: quasi-finite at q (def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime), i.e. pqf-def-quasifinite (1), for every x. Deviation from the letter of 02UR: Stacks goes through 00PK (2) (S_q/pS_q = kappa(q) finite) and the equivalence (2)<=>(1) of 00PK; here (1) is read off the discreteness of the whole fibre, which the proof of 00UW establishes, so no node for 00PK or 00PJ is needed.
